# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. My hands are on the bomb but this turn my view shows only unknowns: wires 1, 2, 3 all unread. I have no tactile reading yet. What does the manual say about this bomb?
Deaf says: I see the bomb. Display shows the number 3. Light is green. Three wires in positions: 1 is red, 2 is green, 3 is blue. Blind, I saw your gesture stop-point-up but cannot hear your words; please describe what you feel. Mute, tell me what the manual says for display 3, green light, wires red-green-blue.

The manual says display 3 with green light → cut red. So the target wire is the red one.

Deaf sees wire 1 is red. Blind needs to cut wire 1. But Blind can't see Deaf's words, and I can't speak — I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf can speak and be heard by Blind. So I must tell Deaf the answer, and Deaf must tell Blind which position to cut.

I'll gesture to Deaf: "cut wire 1" — but Deaf only receives gestures, no words. I need to make a gesture that Deaf can interpret. Since Deaf can hear Blind and speak to Blind, the cleanest path: I gesture the answer to Deaf, and Deaf relays to Blind by voice.

I need to encode "wire 1" in a gesture. I'll use a pointing gesture: 👆 means position 1? Risky — no agreed code. Better: I can gesture the colour? No, Deaf already sees colours. Deaf needs the manual rule. The rule: display 3 + green → red. Deaf can see display=3 and light=green, and sees wire 1 is red. Deaf can figure it out if I confirm the rule.

Let me gesture a clear confirmation: the answer is the red wire. I'll point to indicate "red wire" — but I can't name colour by gesture. I can gesture "1" — one finger up 👆, meaning wire 1. Deaf sees wire 1 is red, and if I signal "1", Deaf can connect: cut wire 1.

I'll gesture 👆 (one) to Deaf, meaning wire 1. And also relay nothing else needed since Deaf can speak to Blind.

Actually, to be safe, I should also make sure Deaf knows the rule maps to red. Deaf already asked me for the manual rule. My gesture 👆 = "one" = wire 1. Deaf sees wire 1 = red. Good.

But wait — can Deaf interpret 👆 as "wire 1"? Ambiguous. I'll send a sequence: 👆 then ✊ (stop/fist = cut)? Still ambiguous. Given constraints, simplest: gesture 👆 to mean the first wire. Deaf is smart and asked for the manual answer; combined with seeing wire 1 is red, and the manual saying green-light display-3 → red, Deaf can conclude.

I'll gesture 👆 to Deaf. Also Deaf must tell Blind to cut wire 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports the bomb: display shows 3, light is green, wires are 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. I still feel nothing concrete yet. What does the manual say for display 3, green light, red-green-blue? Give me the exact cut.
Deaf says: I still see display 3, green light, wires: 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute, you pointed up — does the manual say to cut wire 1? Confirm clearly. Blind, you gave thumbs up — what did you feel? Nobody act until we agree.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋ 👆]

Deaf is asking me to confirm: does the manual say cut wire 1? The manual says display 3, green light → red. Wire 1 is red. So yes, cut wire 1.

I can only gesture to Deaf. I need to confirm "yes, wire 1." A thumbs-up 👍 means yes/affirmative. And 👆 means wire 1. So 👍👆 = "yes, wire 1."

Deaf can then tell Blind to cut wire 1. Blind is the one who can reach the bomb.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👆"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Correction: my thumbs-up was only acknowledgment, not a confirmation of wire 1. I have felt nothing concrete on the bomb. I cannot see your gestures, so I cannot receive the manual from you directly. Please gesture the exact rule to Deaf, and Deaf, speak it to me in words. Nobody cut yet.
Deaf says: Conflict. I see display 3, green light, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signed yes-up, Blind signed no-stop. Mute: confirm — does the manual say cut wire 1, the red top wire? Blind: what do you feel, and which wire can you reach? Nobody act until we agree.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋ 👆]

The manual is unambiguous: display 3, green light → red. Wire 1 is red. The cut is wire 1.

Deaf keeps asking me to confirm. I already gave 👍👆. Deaf is now confused because Blind's thumbs-up was misread as a conflict. I need to be crystal clear. I can only gesture to Deaf. Let me give a strong, unambiguous sequence: 👍 (yes) + 👆 (one) + ✊ (cut/stop-action on it). Actually ✊ might read as "stop." Let me avoid that.

Best: 👍👆 = "yes, wire 1." That's the answer. I'll repeat it emphatically. Deaf then must speak to Blind: "cut wire 1."

I could also point at the red wire specifically, but I can't name colours. Deaf already sees wire 1 is red. The manual rule maps green-light/display-3 to red, and red is wire 1. So 👍👆 is correct and sufficient.

I'll resend 👍👆 clearly. Nothing else I can do.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👆"])
```
